title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 107
paragraphs: So the Spartans waited for the full moon. Meanwhile Hippias son of Pisistratus was guiding the barbarians in to Marathon, having had the previous night a dream in which it seemed to him that he lay with his own mother. From this he concluded that he would return to Athens, recover his rule, and die an old man in his own land. That was how he interpreted the dream. Now, as he was leading the troops in, he first set ashore the slaves from Eretria on the island of Aegleia, belonging to Styra. When the ships came to land at Marathon, he had them moored there, and as the barbarians came ashore he was busy positioning them in their places. While he was doing this, he was seized by a violent fit of sneezing and coughing; and since he was an old man, most of his teeth were loosened by it, and with one great cough he dislodged a tooth. The tooth dropped onto the sand, and he searched eagerly for it; when it could not be found, he groaned and said to those near him: “This land is not ours, nor shall we be able to make it subject. Whatever share of it belonged to me, the tooth has now claimed.”
